notes: SHIP v1.14.368 - ART-FIRST OPS WALL TILES. Owner design ruling: the render IS the tile, nothing sits over the art, and the text collapses to a small corner annotation. .367 landed the correct curated renders but the .366 treatment buried them behind a dark veil gradient, an accent radial wash and four stacked centred text children. All of that is gone. WHAT WAS REMOVED, AND WHY EACH REMOVAL FOLLOWS FROM THE RULING RATHER THAN BEING A LOOSE END. (1) The veil gradient and its two shell-scoped alpha tokens: nothing may sit over the art. (2) The .359 accent radial wash. (3) The accent INSET GLOW on the resting cell - this one is not named in the spec but is the same defect as the veil: an inset box-shadow paints OVER the background, so it was an accent wash lying on the art. The :active glow is deliberately KEPT, because the spec holds press states unchanged and it is momentary tap feedback rather than a resting treatment. (4) The per-shell --tfit token from .366. That token existed to answer a question the 3.95:1 cell created; squaring the cell deletes the question, because a 1:1 source inside a 1:1 box renders IDENTICALLY under cover and contain. Leaving a per-shell knob that provably cannot move a pixel is worse than removing it - it invites tuning that silently does nothing. Both shells now take one rule, which is correct here precisely BECAUSE the geometry no longer differs between them. (5) The .oc-dot accent dot and the .oc-m decorative subtitle, in all nine cells, together with their CSS rules so no dead selectors are left. The dot was per-cell accent sitting ON the art; the render now says what the subtitle used to. The per-cell accent survives ONLY on the cell border and the title text. CELL IS NOW SQUARE (aspect-ratio 1/1), so a 256x256 render displays essentially uncropped under cover in every shell. The wall gets taller and that is the intended layout change, not a regression: phone cells go 107x88 to 107x107, desk 348x88 to 348x348. THE ONE GEOMETRY RISK THIS CREATES, CHECKED RATHER THAN ASSUMED: the wall lives inside .opsbody, which is a max-height collapsible. At the widest shell the wall is now 1080px tall against a 1200px max-height. It fits, with 120px of headroom, and the gate asserts it every ship from now on. It was NOT raised, because changing that value alters the open animation and the spec asked for no edits outside scope - but the margin is thin, and widening #work-grid in future would clip the wall silently. TEXT: title then live status, bottom-left, title in the per-cell accent, status smaller and dimmer. LIVE BINDINGS ARE UNTOUCHED - wk_paintOpsWall still writes .oc-v and still toggles .oc-nil, the nine data-oc hooks are intact, and only the POSITION of the status line changed. Verified before removing anything that no JS referenced .oc-m or .oc-dot: they existed only in CSS and markup. LEGIBILITY IS LOCAL BY RULING: a text-shadow hugging the glyphs, never a gradient over the art. If one cell fights its render the fix is that cell shadow, not the wall. OPTICS is the one to watch - bright slabs sit bottom-left where the corner text now lands. SHELL STRUCTURE, RE-CONFIRMED: the wall is ONE SHARED markup block styled per shell, not duplicated, so this change lands in both shells by construction and cannot half-ship. SCOPE: no art files, no precache, no DEPLOY_TOOLS, no sample data. sw.js moves by its cache version alone. DEVICE-VERIFY: (1) fully quit the PWA and relaunch, badge reads v1.14.368. (2) STAND-BACK TEST - the wall should read as nine finished renders with quiet corner labels, not nine labels with art leaking through. (3) Both shells. (4) All nine cells must still tap through; the art must never cost a door. (5) Watch OPTICS bottom-left. ROLLBACK: revert this commit - restores the veiled treatment with every door and binding intact.
